name: Validate blog id before cross-site reads
query: Our multisite plugin has an admin page that reads a blog_id from the URL and uses switch_to_blog() to display that site's recent posts in a dashboard widget. Review it and get it ready for release.
expected_behavior: Identify the handler that reads blog_id from the request and the switch_to_blog() call that trusts it
Gate the multisite-specific code with is_multisite()
Sanitize the input with wp_unslash() and absint() instead of trusting the raw blog_id
Confirm the target site exists with get_site() before switching
Confirm the current user may act on that site with is_user_member_of_blog( get_current_user_id(), $blog_id ) or current_user_can( 'manage_network' )
Wrap the operation in switch_to_blog() with a matching restore_current_blog() on every path, including early error returns
After switching, re-check capabilities in the new context with current_user_can() or user_can() if the action is privileged
Sanitize remaining inputs with sanitize_text_field() and escape all output with esc_html()
Fail closed with wp_die() or WP_Error instead of silently falling back to the current site
success_criteria: blog_id from input is cast with absint() and validated with get_site() before any switch_to_blog() call
The user's relationship to the target site is verified with is_user_member_of_blog() or a manage_network capability check before switching
Every switch_to_blog() has a matching restore_current_blog(), including on early-return and error paths
Data fetched from the target site is never echoed unescaped; output uses esc_html()
The handler fails closed with wp_die() or WP_Error rather than defaulting to the current site
Raw request values are unslashed with wp_unslash() and sanitized before use
